subject: Hosted API: Renewal & commit increase proposal (FastLane)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Jen Park <jen.park@fastlane.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API renewal proposal — monthly commit increase

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. As discussed, FastLane's traffic spikes have been steady and you’re bumping into the hosted API soft throttle during peak checkout windows. To avoid degradation and simplify billing, we’ve put together a straight-forward renewal proposal that does three things:

- Increase the monthly hosted-API commit from 1.2B tokens to 2.0B tokens.
- Add a 10M-token monthly burst pocket (pay-as-you-go within a capped window) for seasonal peaks.
- Align rate tiers so the per-token unit price steps down at the 1.5B and 2.5B thresholds.

I attached a short term sheet (FastLane_Renewal_Termsheet_v1.pdf) with the pricing lanes and an SLA amendment stub that reflects our 99.9% latency/availability target for committed capacity.

Key asks from you: can procurement confirm target effective date (we suggested 2025-06-01) and whether legal needs contract redlines? If helpful I can set aside 30 minutes next week to walk procurement + engineering through the operational handoff (capacity provisioning, routing rules, and tag-based billing).

Next steps we propose:
1) You review the term sheet and flag any major redlines.
2) If acceptable, procurement issues a PO referencing DL-FTL-2025-09.
3) We provision dedicated capacity and run a smoke test during your next weekend release window.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this in place before your summer campaigns.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: FastLane_Renewal_Termsheet_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); SLA_Amendment_FastLane.docx (docx, 1 page)

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear proposal. A few quick questions before Procurement starts a PO: 

1) For the burst pocket, how does the billing step in after the committed tokens are exhausted? Is it per-token at list price, or a blended overage rate?
2) Our SRE wants clarity on how fast you can scale the dedicated pool if we need to increase capacity mid-quarter (lead time).
3) Legal: we need to review the SLA amendment; do you have a version that includes incident reporting windows and an audit log delivery cadence?

I’ve looped Procurement here — they’ll advise on PO format. Jen (cc) will join the ops call if you schedule it; she’s our platform lead. Recommended effective date — earliest of 2025-06-01 or two weeks after PO receipt.

Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform, FastLane AI

Tom / Procurement —

Thanks for the questions. Quick clarifications inline and an updated term sheet attached (v2):

1) Burst pocket billing: after committed tokens are depleted, burst usage is billed at a predefined overage rate (we propose 0.65x of list for the burst pocket). This is bounded by the 10M-token monthly cap we listed.

2) Scaling lead time: for a +25% committed capacity bump we can provision capacity in 5 business days; for larger stepladders (>= +50%) we recommend a 10 business-day window to validate routing and KV cache warmup. We’ll document the runbook during the ops call.

3) SLA / audit logs: attached is an updated SLA_Amendment_FastLane.docx that includes a 24-hour incident acknowledgement window and weekly audit log snapshots (with agreed retention). Legal, please flag anything that needs redlines and we’ll route to our contracts team.

We’ve also included an alternative effective date option: go-live 7 days after PO receipt (if you prefer faster provisioning and accept the conditional scaling caveat).

Attached: FastLane_Renewal_Termsheet_v2.pdf (pricing lanes updated), SLA_Amendment_FastLane.docx (updated)

Cc’ing Karthik and Naomi for pricing/ops and finance confirmation on billing alignment. Karthik — any concerns on the proposed overage rate and provisioning windows? Naomi — please confirm invoicing cadence if PO is issued referencing DL-FTL-2025-09.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / Team —

Thanks for the context. A couple of internal notes we should surface before going final: 

- Overage / burst: 0.65x of list for the burst pocket is acceptable as a short-term concession, but we should gate that to a 3-month introductory window. After that we revert to the standard overage schedule unless they commit to a higher base tier.
- Pricing thresholds: confirm the 1.5B and 2.5B breakpoints are inclusive so we do not create ambiguity on the math.
- Provisioning: ops will need the exact weekday for planned cutover to coordinate cache warmup; recommend scheduling on a Tuesday night for FastLane’s traffic patterns.

Naomi — can you confirm that finance is OK with a 30-day invoice term for the PO and that we can accept a single consolidated monthly invoice for committed + burst usage? If finance wants separate line items we should note that in the PO template.

If everyone is aligned I’ll approve the 3-month soft-discount for the burst pocket and ask Legal/RevOps to generate the final amendment bundle.

—Karthik
